options.metric: Annual count of motorist deaths in police-reported crashes
options.reason: Annual deaths directly describe the fatality burden recorded by this crash dataset without implying an exposure-adjusted risk.
options.answer: Recorded motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025 (-26.4%), but this does not establish a decline in deaths per mile driven.
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether the annual count of recorded motorist deaths changed, and the chart shows a lower total in 2025 than in 2013. It is defensible as a measure of fatality burden in the crash records. It leaves the per-mile risk question unanswered because the data contain no miles driven.

options.metric: Motorist-fatal crash records per 100,000 police-reported crash records
options.denominator: All police-reported crash records in the year
options.reason: A crash-denominated rate indicates how often a recorded crash involved a motorist death while making its denominator explicit.
options.answer: Motorist-fatal crash records increased from 50.1 to 87.7 per 100,000 reported crashes between 2013 and 2025 (75.1%), not a per-mile risk estimate.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how the occurrence of motorist-fatal crashes compares with the volume of all reported crashes, and the chart shows this ratio was higher in 2025 than in 2013. It is defensible as a crash-level descriptive ratio, not an individual motorist exposure rate. It leaves deaths per mile driven unanswered because neither miles nor the number of motorists exposed is recorded.

answer:
Recorded motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025 (26.4%), but this crash-data count does not establish a decline in per-mile risk; [chart](out/option_1.png) · [values](out/values_1.csv).

Motorist-fatal crashes rose from 50.1 to 87.7 per 100,000 reported crashes over the same period, a crash-level ratio that also does not establish per-mile risk; [chart](out/option_2.png) · [values](out/values_2.csv).
